content:
Recently, I had the opportunity to visit the Cyber Centre of Excellence, Gujarat Police, where I witnessed how technology, digital forensics, and inter-agency coordination are strengthening cybercrime investigations across India. It was an insightful experience that reinforced the importance of collaboration between law enforcement, financial institutions, and legal professionals in combating cyber-enabled financial fraud.
Recent cyber fraud investigations have also highlighted a growing concern. Many innocent individuals find their bank accounts frozen after receiving an unknown payment. In several cases, fraudsters move stolen funds through multiple bank accounts as part of a complex money trail. If such funds are traced to an account during an investigation, the Cyber Police may direct the bank to impose a Debit Freeze or Lien Hold to preserve evidence and prevent further movement of funds.
It is important to understand that receiving an unknown payment does not automatically make someone an accused. The investigation focuses on whether the account holder had any connection with the transaction, whether there was a legitimate business or personal purpose behind it, and whether sufficient documentary evidence exists to support that explanation.
If you ever receive an unexpected or unexplained payment, avoid using, withdrawing, or transferring the amount. Preserve all relevant documents, including invoices, agreements, chat records, and bank statements, and cooperate fully with the investigating authorities. If you are an innocent account holder facing financial hardship due to a prolonged account freeze, appropriate legal remedies are available to seek the unfreezing of the account.
This visit was a reminder that while cybercrime is becoming increasingly sophisticated, legal awareness and responsible banking practices remain equally important in protecting individuals from unnecessary legal complications.

Advocate Sunita Sharma

comment: Account freezes often create a difficult balance between preserving investigation evidence and protecting genuine account holders. Clear timelines and transparent communication channels can significantly reduce hardship for innocent parties.
